𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 | 𝟖𝟓𝐭𝐡 𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐱𝐡𝐢𝐛𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 – 𝐍𝐚𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲

In exercise of the powers conferred upon me under section 21 (1) (b) of the Hyderabad City Police Act, 1348 Fasli, I. V.C .Sajjanar, IPS., Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad City, do hereby notify, for information of the general public that, in order to facilitate better traffic regulation and management, in view of the 85th All India Industrial Exhibition to be held at the Exhibition Grounds, Nampally, Hyderabad, the following traffic restrictions will be enforced from 01-01-2026 to 15-02-2026 from 1600 hours till midnight everyday. 

1. RTC District Buses, Private Buses and Heavy Vehicles coming from SA bazaar and Jambagh side and intending to go towards Nampally side will be diverted at MJ Market  towards Abids junction.

2. RTC District Buses, Private Buses, and Heavy Vehicles coming from Police Control Room & Basheer Bagh and intending to go towards Nampally will be diverted at AR Petrol Pump and BJR Statue towards Abids. 

3.The Heavy and Medium Motor Vehicles coming from Begum Bazar Chatri and intending to go towards Malakunta will be diverted at Alaska junction towards Darusalam and Ek minar, Nampally.

4. The Heavy and Medium Motor Vehicles including DCM vehicles coming from Darusalam (Goshamahal Road) and intending to go towards Afzalgunj or Abids will be diverted at Alaska junction towards Begum Bazar, City College and Nayapool.

5.The Heavy and Medium Motor Vehicles including RTC busses coming from Moosa Bowli/Bahadurpura side and intending to go towards Nampally will be diverted at City College towards Nayapool & MJ Market.

6. In view of the 85th All India Industrial Exhibition, the commuters are requested to avoid the route of MJ Market – Gandhi Bhavan – Nampally junction especially between 4 p.m. and 12 midnight everyday till 15.02.2026 and take alternative routes to reach their destination.

7.The citizens intending to visit the Exhibition are requested to avail the public transport facilities like RTC buses and Metro Rail services (available till 11.30 p.m. on weekdays and 12 midnight on weekends and public holidays) and help in reducing traffic congestion in the surroundings of Exhibition Ground.

8.The visitors to the Exhibition are advised to avoid crossing the road as it can be dangerous.  They are advised to use the Gandhi Bhavan Metro Bridge and Metro Lift/Elevator to cross the road.

Citizens are requested to co-operate with the police personnel on duty.

V.C.Sajjanar.,
Commissioner of Police,
Hyderabad City

Worldwide Wednesday is back — and this week’s global military + geopolitics rundown is stacked. China’s “Justice Mission 2025” drills are encircling Taiwan, the U.S. and Philippines are running major joint exercises near South China Sea flashpoints, and Taiwan Marines are testing sea-launched loitering munitions (“suicide drones”). Meanwhile Japan just approved a record defense budget aimed at deterring China, and Europe’s air defense pipeline keeps moving as France’s next-gen SAMP/T NG system passes a live-fire test.

We also cover Iran launching three satellites from Russia (a deeper Tehran–Moscow space tie), Belarus receiving new Russian Su-30SM2 fighters, and a Ukraine drone strike on a Russian Black Sea terminal that hits Kazakhstan’s export flows. On the sanctions front, the U.S. targets a Colombian network accused of recruiting mercenaries for Sudan’s war, and India and the U.S. push for more UN terrorism listings.

Watch to the end and drop your take: which story changes the next 90 days the most? #military #veteran #nato #brics #geopolitics
